title: How an asphalt driveway is built
caption: Your driveway is rocks glued together with crude oil 🛣️ #howitsbuilt #driveway #asphalt #homeowner #howitworks

lines.text: If you drive on your lawn every day, you get two deep, muddy ruts.
So you dig out the soft topsoil, because it squishes and settles.
But the dirt underneath still turns to mud every time it rains.
So you spread a thick layer of crushed *stone*, and a roller packs it down tight.
Now you have a gravel driveway.
But tires kick the gravel around, and every storm washes it into ruts.
So you pave it with *asphalt*: rocks and sand glued together with *bitumen*, a sticky black goo made from crude oil.
You lay it in two layers: a rough bottom coat, then a smoother top coat.
It comes out of the truck at about *three hundred degrees*, and gets rolled flat while it's still hot.
But if it's dead flat, rain just sits on top of it.
So you tilt it slightly, and the water runs off into the grass.
But the sun slowly bakes the goo until it turns gray and brittle.
And in winter, water seeps into tiny cracks, freezes, and expands.
Every freeze pries the cracks a little wider, until chunks break loose.
So every few years you fill the cracks and paint on a *sealcoat*, which keeps out the sun and the water.
